utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning. This is Case Number IT-98-33-A, the Prosecutor versus Radislav Krstic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Appearances for the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAKER
utterances.text: May it please Your Honour, my name is Christopher Staker. I appear on behalf of the Prosecution with our case manager Mr. Wolfgang Sakulin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. For General Krstic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my name is Nenad Petrusic. I'm appearing for General Krstic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. And General Krstic, are you able to hear the proceedings in a language which you understand? There's no need to stand up.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Yes, I can. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: First of all, I would like to apologise to the Prosecution, but I decided we should proceed with it because the rules require it. If there's anything that the Prosecution want to add, those who are handling the matter, please get in touch with my legal officer and we will organise something for you. This is a Status Conference called in accordance with the provisions of the rules. Is there anything that you do wish to raise, Mr. Staker?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAKER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, there's nothing the Prosecution would wish to raise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Petrusic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, the Defence has nothing to raise. If you consider it necessary, we can inform the Court what point we have reached under Rule 68 and 66, that is, discovery, according to Mr. Farrell's communication. We expect this process to be completed by the middle of this month when we shall probably have a meeting and discuss this problem in detail. And I hope solve it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: When you say the middle of this month, do you mean the middle of September? We're already well past the middle of this month. So that means that you are hopefully approaching some form of agreement about the further discovery that you sought?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, sir, thank you for your correction, Your Honour. I did mean September.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Assuming for the moment that you do reach that agreement, you'll then have to apply your mind to any application you want to make for additional evidence to be considered. And that's a matter which is becoming of some importance if we are able to dispose of this appeal speedily, or at least more speedily than it has been so far.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I fully agree with you. And in my estimation, unlike the previous quantity of material received by the Defence in February and March, this time, the material will not be so voluminous, and the Defence will need less time to carry out its inspection and search of the material and proceed within the time limit of 60 days to inform the Chamber of our further work on this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm not sure that the 60 days is the same 60 days that I have in my mind. I recall that it was thought it would take 60 days some time last year in order to file a status report. You don't have 60 more days in which to gather together your application to admit additional evidence. Hopefully, you'll be -- you should be getting on to that with material you've already got, and of course any further material that comes in, you can add to it. But we will expect you to make your application, if any application is to be made, to admit additional evidence very much more speedily than 60 days after you've completed the discovery.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am starting from the assumption that an agreement will be reached between the Prosecution and the Defence. Of course, I agree with you that the material that has already been discovered, that this material has already been looked at by the Defence, and I agree that the time limit should be shorter in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: The time limit has recently been amended to I think it's 75 days after the date of final judgement. That doesn't apply in these proceedings, of course. But nevertheless you can see that the Tribunal is very concerned about the time that it takes to consider these applications. It's a very difficult process, and when you do make your application, I hope you will give us assistance by identifying the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. particular ground of appeal or finding of fact or law by the Trial Chamber to which each piece of evidence applies. It's not easy for people who are not involved in the trial to be able to consider applications for new evidence. The Prosecution, of course, has the right to reply, and they may have some difficulty with that material supplied under Rule 68. But nevertheless, they may have very valid objections to some of the other material, so we want to get on with this as soon as we can. That's why I am trying to encourage you to start compiling material even now, seeing that you have had most of it since the beginning of this year. So if you would keep that in mind. I don't want to make any orders at this stage. But at some stage when we have your next status report as to the progress of the discovery, we will have to at that stage impose time limits so that we can get on with the case. Is there anything else you want to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is nothing I wish to raise, Your Honour. I would only like to say that I assure you that in relation to the material already received, the Defence is already working on its submission under Rule 115 so that we will be in an advanced phase in preparing our submission when we receive the new material, and this will be included in the report that we shall submit to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm very grateful to hear that, Mr. Petrusic. I'm glad that you're getting on with it. These appeals are starting to string out, not through any fault of the parties. I can understand the problems that you face. But these further discovery problems and the further revelation by some government authorities are starting to bog the Appeals Chamber down in no uncertain terms. But thank you very much for your assurance. Mr. Staker, I know you can't deal with this, but there was some discussion with Mr. Farrell at an earlier Status Conference about what attitude the Appeals Chamber should take to this very troublesome problem of Rule 68. And I just want to remind the Prosecution that that is a matter which the Appeals Chamber may very well still wish to pursue even if the -- there is an agreement finally as to the further disclosure. There was a document signed by the -- by some of the counsel who took part in the trial identifying the basis upon which they took the view that certain material was not discoverable under Rule 68. Some of the assertions made in that document were very hotly disputed by the Defence. And Mr. Farrell very wisely suggested, and everybody agreed, that those disputed issues should not be dealt with until the whole of the discovery had been completed because there may be other issues. But Mr. Farrell, I think, very properly agreed that the interpretation of Rule 68 and some of the practical problems involved in it is a matter which is ripe for some sort of consideration in the course of this appeal so that I want to remind the Prosecution that that is an issue that still has to be dealt with. I think it would be most properly dealt with in the course of the appeal itself. Right, is there anything more to say with respect to what Mr. Petrusic said?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAKER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you very much for coming along, Mr. Staker. I understand the problems you had. I apologise once again for the breakdown in the communication chain, but it did happen at my end, not yours. Thank you for coming. And I'll now adjourn.
